value.type: the jth standard basis vector of ℝⁿ
value.declaration: Let v_j be the jth standard basis vector in ℝⁿ.

patches.value: Fix arbitrary r>0 and spatial index j∈Fin n; define v_j=e_j, f_j(x)=∂_{x_j}u(x,r), and g(x)=u_t(x,r). N001 directly supplies a closed time window containing r and a compact C outside which u=q throughout that window. Because u is jointly smooth and is constant on the open set (ℝⁿ\C)×J, f_j,g and their Frechet derivatives vanish outside C and are continuous. Thus the three functions ⟨Df_j(x)[v_j],g(x)⟩, ⟨f_j(x),Dg(x)[v_j]⟩, and ⟨f_j(x),g(x)⟩ are continuous and supported in C. By M001, once the ambient finite-on-compacts property proved in R002 is instantiated, all three are integrable. Smoothness gives the Frechet derivative identities everywhere, in particular on tsupport(g) for f_j and tsupport(f_j) for g. Apply M011 with X=ℝⁿ, F=G=ℝᵐ, W=ℝ, B the Euclidean dot product and direction v_j. It gives ∫⟨∂_{x_j}u,∂_{x_j}u_t⟩=−∫⟨∂_{x_jx_j}u,u_t⟩. Since j was arbitrary, sum these identities over j=1,…,n. The finite-dimensional product rule yields ∫e_t=2∫u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu). N002 identifies E′(r)=∫e_t, proving N003 for arbitrary r>0.
